case.selection_basis: Default per task card. Selected on evidence fit: primary SEC filings give separately-reported cash and restricted cash, a full 9M cash-flow split, dated debt terms and a quantified cost action all published before the cutoff. Appgate/WeWork were not re-examined in this run; no later outcome was used to choose.

cutoff.first_reveal: S8 issuer-public 2024-02-12T16:01:00-05:00 (SEC acceptance of the same 8-K at 16:09:41, S3); first reveal is the earlier
cutoff.stale_interval: 2023-09-30 to 2023-11-10 has no reported balance; any estimate there is a nowcast, identical across baseline and response branches
cutoff.availability_note: Q4 issuer-public time precedes SEC availability by 8 min 41 s; both are after cutoff and held out

baseline_B1.description: Carry 9M operating and investing cash flows forward at one-third per quarter; assume zero financing and FX (the 9M financing outflow was dominated by a one-time $187.0M term loan repayment, per S2). Revolver draws and portfolio-management collection timing are not modelled.
baseline_B1.note: Computed here only to define the method. Scoring against H03 belongs to the historical run, not to evidence.

debt_rule_R1.description: A Domino alert rule: flag a debt event when its date enters a 12-month look-forward from the as-of date. 2025-01-01 (revolver) and 2025-01-30 (term loan) enter the window for as-of dates on or after 2024-01-01 and 2024-01-30. At the 2023-11-10 cutoff both are outside it, so R1 would not fire on them; it is a policy being demonstrated, not a reconstruction of when anyone first warned.
historical_facts_not_derived_from_r1: F30: the company's own 10-Q (2023-11-09) already warned that liquidity may not suffice if the term loan accelerates to 2025-01-30
F18: the revolver springing termination on 2025-01-01 (>$50M of 2025 Notes) is earlier than the term-loan date and was also in the 10-Q
F31: management said on 2023-11-09 it was in active discussions to refinance the converts
H10 (held out): going-concern conditional language first seen in the 2024-02-12 release

management_expectation_vs_warning.expectation: F32 (portfolio management cash $145M over 12-24 months; MD&A 12-month statement not retrieved)

debt_rule_R1.caveat: Legal reading of the credit agreement not verified; thresholds ($50M revolver / $40M term loan) are reader-extracted from Note 8. No claim that R1 would have been an early or unique signal.

intervention_A1.label: Bounded second cost action
intervention_A1.description: HYPOTHETICAL bounded second cost action. Not a company plan or disclosed intention. Sized as a fraction of an expected (not realised) Q3 action.

anchors.note: 55,000/12 = 4,583.33 rounded; anchor is a management expectation (F17), not realised savings

headcount_reduction_percent.basis: analyst range, 25%-50% of the Q3 action

one_time_cash_cost_as_fraction_of_annual.basis: upper end is the Q3 charge/savings ratio (F14/F17), which includes non-cash and lease items so cash cost may be lower; low end is analyst

first_cash_savings_lag_quarters.basis: analyst; Q3 action only began to show in later quarters. No evidence found of realised timing

savings_cash_conversion.basis: analyst; public expense savings are not automatically cash

revenue_or_enrollment_downside.basis: Not evidenced. S7 reports Q3 FCE enrollments -21%, attributed to portfolio management and a mid-2022 marketing change, so public data does not isolate any effect of headcount on revenue.

gross_savings_offset_fraction.basis: hypothetical: share of gross annualized savings lost to lower revenue contribution or added attrition cost; 0 and 0.5 are analyst bounds, not estimates

revenue_at_risk_pct_of_fy2023_revenue_gu.basis: hypothetical bound; midpoint of $965-990M (F26). 1.0% = 9,775 thousand per year at the upper bound. Timing unknown

revenue_or_enrollment_downside.label: hypothetical analyst sensitivity; must be shown as an unknown range, never a forecast

intervention_A1.feasibility: UNKNOWN. The Q3 2023 12% headcount cut and its expected $55M annualized savings (F16, F17) are management statements; realised savings and cash timing are not evidenced. Nothing here treats the prior cut as proof that a further cut would save money or can be executed. Consent, severance law, university-contract delivery obligations, covenants (including minimum Recurring Revenues, F23) and noteholder talks (F31) were not examined.
intervention_A1.in_window_implication: Cost lands before savings. With a 1-2 quarter lag the 2023-12-31 target is likely flat or lower in cash than baseline, and the benefit appears in 2024. This is analyst reasoning, not evidence.
intervention_A1.caution: Alternatives must be chosen/frozen before reveal. A1 is predeclared here before any run.

gross_annualized_savings.calc: 4,583.33 per headcount point (55,000/12) x 3 or 6 points

cash_savings_inside_window_to_2023-12-31.calc: lag of 1-2 quarters from a cutoff-date announcement lands savings after 2023-12-31

cash_effect_inside_window.calc: one-time cost only; revenue downside unknown and excluded

annualized_net_savings_after_downside_an.calc: high = 100% conversion, 0 offset. Low is unknown: with offset and severance-driven revenue loss the net could be negative, so no floor is asserted

bounded_arithmetic_thousands.status: arithmetic on predeclared hypothetical ranges; not a forecast; cents = thousands x 100000 when loaded

hindsight_experiment_X1.description: January 2024 factoring of up to $86.2M receivables at 88% (H11). Not available as a cutoff input: counterparty, rate and capacity unknown before 2024-02-12. May be shown only as a separately labelled hindsight experiment.

rules: No weekly actuals, invoices or payroll are present or implied.
EBITDA/revenue are never converted to cash.
Restricted cash is always carried separately; F03 and H03 are the only combined totals and are reported by the issuer.
